title: Cost of the bounded-family Fourier estimator
statement: Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a sign-valued target, let $\mathcal F$ be any finite family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $0<\varepsilon\le1/2$, and let $M$ be a positive integer. For every outcome in the support of the estimator that uses $m$ samples per family member, where $m$ is its bounded-family sample count, the cost is exactly $(|\mathcal F|m,\,0,\,|\mathcal F|m+|\mathcal F|m(n+1))$, recording random examples, queries, and local work, respectively.
hypotheses_covered: The target is a function from the $n$-dimensional sign cube to the signs
$\mathcal F$ is a finite family of subsets of an $n$-element set
The outcome lies in the estimator's probability support
